blockers.title: Regression: on a tight crop (no page layout), F1's new particles make a surname with an unknown two-letter interior word READY and wrong, with that word silently dropped from the reading
blockers.location: src/capabilities/studentScan.ts:880-896 (interiorNameSpan runs over nameParts that nameTokensFromWords already filtered when layout is null); src/capabilities/studentScan.ts:238-247 (new lo/li/el/al particles)
blockers.scenario: Probe (scratchpad/review-probes/f1/base-probe2.mts, fictitious names): a two-row crop, so fewer than 3 structured rows and no layout. Rows are 'Lo Re Marco' and 'Verdani Giulia'. At 5c1e029 the result was first 'Marco', surname '' and not ready (flagged). With F1 the order is surname-given, surname 'Lo', first 'Marco', raw 'Lo Marco', compoundAmbiguity false, candidateIsReady true. 'Li Wu Anna' behaves the same: surname 'Li', ready. 'Del Re Marco' was already ready as 'Del' at base and is unchanged. The full-sheet (layout) path does flag 'Lo Re Marco' (droppedInteriorWord true). The self-review's SC-4 claim ('an unknown short word inside a name stays in the reading and marks the split') is therefore false for tight crops and pages with few rows. A minor's surname is stored wrong, silently.
blockers.suggestedFix: In the no-layout words path, compute interiorNameSpan from the unfiltered tokens of the words outside the structured ranges, as the layout path already does. Set droppedInteriorWord/compoundAmbiguity from that. Add table tests for crops with fewer than 3 structured rows ('Lo Re', 'Del Re', 'Li Wu', both orders).

blockers.title: RR-4 is reported as done but the public repository still serves the unrewritten history. The only rewrite is an unpushed scratch mirror that still holds the old refs, and F1 is built on the old history
blockers.scenario: `git ls-remote origin` returns main ef7cdd8, codex/0.3.0 82d1bc0, codex/post-mvp-ux-planning 8e9b2b7 and tag v0.2.0 bdab05d. These are the exact SHAs RR-4 audited as containing real names and birth dates. The local main reflog shows no rewrite. The only rewritten history is scratchpad/mirror-test.git (main 100e10b, whose tree is identical to 5c1e029; tag 8accdd9), with remote.origin.mirror=true. In that mirror refs/heads/claude/* still point to the unrewritten 5c1e029, from which the old v0.2.0 commit is reachable, and refs/remotes/* and refs/codex/* are old too. claude/f1 sits on 5c1e029. The tracked doc nevertheless says the history 'was replaced … verified by a whole-history scan (0 remaining)'. Minors' data therefore remains public while the docs say otherwise. Pushing F1 as a branch, or pushing the mirror with --mirror, would keep or republish the old objects.
blockers.suggestedFix: Change the doc to say the rewrite is prepared and not pushed. Before any push: carry F1 onto the rewritten 100e10b line. Delete claude/*, refs/remotes/* and refs/codex/* from the mirror. Force-push only the rewritten main, codex/* and tag, never --mirror. Re-run the whole-history scan on a fresh clone of the remote, then do the GitHub purge.

blockers.title: A false PASS can still be recorded: a stray .only narrows the local run and the recorder accepts it (residual of RR-2)
blockers.location: playwright.config.ts:13 (forbidOnly only when CI); vitest.config.ts (allowOnly defaults to !CI); scripts/record-verification.mjs:57 (children spawned without CI); eslint.config.js (no focused-test rule)
blockers.scenario: Leave `test.only` in any e2e spec, or `it.only` in a unit file, and run `npm run evidence -- <ID>`. Playwright runs only the focused test across the whole suite, and Vitest skips the rest of that file. Both exit 0. verification.json gets the recorder id, every declared script with exitCode 0 and a matching sourceDigest, and `milestone:complete` accepts it. CI would reject the .only, but milestone closure does not depend on CI.
blockers.suggestedFix: Set forbidOnly: true and Vitest allowOnly: false, or pass CI=1 into the recorder's child environment. Add a self-test refusal case with a focused test.

importantFindings.title: The update banner's Aggiorna reloads the app without asking the leave guard, so it discards an unsaved scan review, an open evaluation note, a failed evaluation save or a pending edit
importantFindings.scenario: Review 40 scanned rows, or open a Valutazioni note, then tap Aggiorna, which is always visible while an update waits. updateServiceWorker(true) reloads with no confirmation, and the work the guards protect on Back and the bottom navigation is lost.
importantFindings.suggestedFix: onUpdate={() => requestLeave(() => void updateServiceWorker(true))}, so the existing guards ask first.

importantFindings.title: Regression: a student-section heading that carries an age, date or phone no longer ends personnel mode, so every following student is silently dropped
importantFindings.scenario: Probe (base-probe.mts versus parser-probe.mts): a 'Personale' heading, one staff row, then the heading 'Allievi (8-12 anni)' and 3 student rows. 5c1e029 gives 3 candidates. F1 gives 0, and the sheet shows 'Immagine poco leggibile'. With students above the staff block, the ones after the heading would disappear without a trace. The trigger depends on the sheet layout.
importantFindings.suggestedFix: Apply the pure-heading rule only when entering personnel mode. Any STUDENT_SECTION keyword line should end it, because that is the safe direction; staff rows are still flagged by role code.

importantFindings.title: SC-12 residual: a student whose name is a keyword (Domenica, Sabato, Corso, Stampa) is still silently dropped when the age word is not read
importantFindings.scenario: Probe: 'Bardino Domenica 3331234567 12 annl 01/02/2014', with the age word misread, in a 4-row sheet gives 3 candidates and no trace of the row. The fix only helps when AGE_PATTERN matches. A roster without an age column fails the same way.
importantFindings.suggestedFix: When a layout exists and the line has name-cell words left of a date or phone, skip the keyword test or keep the row flagged, and report skipped lines.

importantFindings.title: After this update the first dictation needs the network again: pinning the model revision and moving to the local ORT runtime invalidate every existing speech cache
importantFindings.location: src/capabilities/speech.ts:74,299; node_modules/@huggingface/transformers/src/utils/hub.js:139-146 (browser cache key = remote URL including /resolve/{revision}/); vite.config.ts runtimeCaching (the ~26 MB ORT wasm is runtime-cached, not precached)
importantFindings.scenario: A phone that cached whisper-base under 'main' and the jsDelivr runtime updates the app, then goes offline, for example at sea. At the first dictation the cache is missed for both the model and the new hashed ORT assets, prepare fails, and the user sees 'Dettatura non riuscita' with no hint.
importantFindings.suggestedFix: Add 'dictation after update, offline' to the UG2 device checklist. Pre-warm speech after an update while online, or offer a download step. Show an 'internet needed once' message on an offline prepare failure.

importantFindings.title: F1's tree is mixed with in-progress V05 code that has FAIL review blockers, and it was edited during this review and during the verify:all run
importantFindings.location: src/features/students/StudentScan.tsx (imports untracked StudentScanAssistant.tsx and rosterPaste.ts); src/capabilities/studentScanReview.ts ('from-assistant' rule); .evidence/V05/review-round-1.json (FAIL: V5-1, V5-2)
importantFindings.scenario: StudentScan.tsx changed at 18:19 (1557→1741 lines while I read it), StudentScanAssistant.tsx at 18:15, studentScanReview.ts at 18:05 and rosterPaste.ts at 18:04. All of these are after the F1 self-review (17:39). The F1 checkpoint cannot build without V05 files, and the F1 self-review never covers them. The digest check will refuse completion on the moving tree, which is correct.
importantFindings.suggestedFix: Close V05 (domain re-review PASS) before the F1 checkpoint, or make F1 build without V05 files. Then re-record F1 verification and update the self-review on the final tree.

qolFindings.title: The row swap clears the dropped-interior-word flag
qolFindings.scenario: On a full sheet, 'Lo Re Marco' has words [Lo, Marco] with droppedInteriorWord. A tap on swap sets twoWordReading to true, acknowledged to true, and the compound flag disappears.

qolFindings.title: Restoring a held Back with forward() and a 1 s window is fragile
qolFindings.scenario: A desktop Forward, or a multi-step back via history.go(-n) or the long-press back menu, is 'restored' by a single forward(), so the screen and the history entry diverge. If the forward popstate arrives more than 1 s late (main thread busy, for example ORT transcription while the note guard holds), it is treated as a new Back and re-arms the window, which can swallow the next real Back.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Recognise the restore popstate by an entry id or depth in state rather than by time, and restore with history.go(delta).

qolFindings.title: Escape or phone Back closes the crew-copy confirmation while the copy is saving, and the replacement still happens
qolFindings.scenario: Tap Sostituisci, then press Back during the write. The dialog closes and the crews are replaced anyway.

qolFindings.title: The update banner cannot be dismissed and sits over the bottom ~4 rem above the navigation
qolFindings.scenario: While an update waits, the crew workspace's quick-access rail and the bottom controls are partly covered on every screen.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Add a dismiss, or reserve its height in the layout.

qolFindings.title: History entries of an erased course stay reachable
qolFindings.scenario: Erase the course, press phone Back on the course-creation screen, then create a new course. AppShell opens on the old entry, for example Settings, or Allievi with an erased studentToOpen. This is harmless but confusing.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Always replace the current entry with a fresh home entry when AppShell mounts after creation, or store the course id in shell entries.

qolFindings.title: No artifact or regression guard proves the RR-6 claim that a first dictation makes no jsDelivr request
qolFindings.scenario: The self-review asserts 'a recorded first dictation made no jsDelivr request', but no test or evidence file contains that recording.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Add a browser or offline check that fails on any cdn.jsdelivr.net request during a fixture dictation, or record the network log.
